findings.detail: Commit 9577b03 fixed generated product SKUs escaping duplicate detection by registering `randomSku` into `skuSet` (line ~357). The sibling branch that generates `Pack${n}-${Math.floor(Math.random()*1000000)}` for an empty pack SKU does not do the same. Because pack columns are reached through `mapping['sku']` only when non-empty, a generated pack SKU is written into `row[cIdx]` after the `field.key === 'sku'` pass has already seen the cell as blank — so it is never keyed, never in `taken`, and never deduped. That is the exact birthday-collision case the commit message says should no longer ship silently (~39% odds across 1,000 blank pack SKUs), just on the other branch. Narrow enough to be low: it needs two blanks to draw the same 6-digit value.
findings.summary: Generated pack SKUs skip the duplicate registry the PR just added

findings.detail: `mapDataToTemplate([stripped], …)` is now called once per row instead of once per sheet, so `isRewaaTemplate(templateHeaders)` and `headerFor(templateHeaders, 'variant name')` are recomputed for every row. `matchesTemplate` compounds it: for each of ~60 template headers it calls `resolveSourceKey(h, keys)`, which builds a fresh `Map` over all the row's keys — so the audit columns cost O(headers × keys) per row, per template, and both `auditSimple` and `auditVar` can be on at once. OCR batches are typically hundreds of rows, not tens of thousands, so this is well short of a freeze; it becomes a real problem only if OCR output volume grows.
findings.summary: Template mapping and the audit check rebuild their header indexes per row

findings.detail: The newly added helper declares `wb: any`, `toExportRow: (row: any[]) => any[]`, and `const issueData: any[][]`. These are new lines, not reindented legacy, and none carries a justification comment. `wb: any` is the one that costs something concretely: `wb.SheetNames.map(...)` and the `XLSX_STYLE.utils.book_append_sheet(wb, ...)` call are both unchecked, so a future rename or a wrong argument order compiles clean and fails at export time — the exact path a user only discovers as a corrupt download.

Previously a barcode matching an SKU was only *reported*; it is now renamed on every occurrence, because the SKU claims the base code. Retail catalogues commonly set barcode == SKU deliberately across the whole file — in that case this PR rewrites the entire barcode column to `X-1`, `X-2`, … in one pass. This is deliberate, documented (MODULE_GUIDE 'Duplicates since 2026-09-28'), surfaced in the in-app auto-fix list, and recorded per row in the Change Log as `Resolved Barcode = SKU`, so it is not hidden and the source file is untouched. Raising this as an observation only: the pre-PR behaviour already treated the condition as an error, so auto-fixing is consistent — but the blast radius on a barcode==SKU catalogue is the whole column, and that is worth an explicit product-owner nod alongside D8.
findings.summary: Barcode-equals-SKU is now silently auto-rewritten on every occurrence
